name: SpaceX orbital data center satellite (AI sat, estimate)
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'SpaceX AI Satellites' type (a million-satellite dawn-dusk disk). Body frame: +Z to the Sun, +X toward nadir. SpaceX has published orbits, not hardware: every dimension and material is an estimate sized to the legacy type. Kept small (a handful of lobes) because a million satellites fly it.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: arrays face the Sun (+Z), +X toward nadir; arrays tilted off the Sun by the global flare-mitigation slider
sources.source: SpaceX 'Orbital Data Center System' application to the FCC, filed 2026-01-30 (accepted for filing, FCC DA 26-113; SpaceNews 2026-01-31): up to one million solar-powered satellites, 500-2000 km, 30 deg and sun-synchronous inclinations, optical inter-satellite links. No attitude is published; this is the v1.1 legacy type's SunTrackingTilted law (SatelliteSim.cpp legacyAttitudeGroup), which a dawn-dusk, near-constant-sunlight orbit favours.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: 3 x 4 x 1.5 m aluminium box, sun-pointing (a Starlink V3-class bus)
sources.source: SpaceX 'Orbital Data Center System' application to the FCC, filed 2026-01-30 (accepted for filing, FCC DA 26-113; SpaceNews 2026-01-31): up to one million solar-powered satellites, 500-2000 km, 30 deg and sun-synchronous inclinations, optical inter-satellite links - no hardware dimensions. Estimate; range +-50%.

sources.subject: array
sources.value: both wings on one group, tilted about -Y by the flare-mitigation slider
two 8 x 30 m rigid glass-covered wings (480 m2, near the legacy type's 600 m2 cross-section)
sources.source: Sized to the v1.1 legacy type (cross_section_m2 600, mirror_frac 0.5 = glassy arrays). No published size.

sources.value: two 12 x 3 m white radiators in the Sun-nadir plane (edge-on to both), 72 m2
sources.source: The legacy type's SunPerp secondary (radiators edge-on to the Sun, weight 0.18 of the arrays). Area and coating are estimates; compute satellites need large radiators, so this may be low.
